title.purpose: Modal headers and topic group headers.

headline.purpose: The header's live date and the week-range dates.

body.purpose: Task titles, default copy, and field input text.

label.purpose: Tabs, chips, search, toggles, control labels, field captions. Also covers the 9-11px uppercase eyebrow variant used for badges, flags, and section titles.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Task-card hover only; the sole resting-state shadow exception.

shadows.name: overlay-lift
shadows.purpose: Modal, floating over a rgba(0,0,0,0.45) backdrop scrim.

motion.name: fade-quick
motion.purpose: Drag-handle and row-action opacity reveals on hover; the only motion in the system.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one filled, high-emphasis action (e.g. '+ Add').
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-text); border: 1px solid var(--accent); cursor: pointer; transition: filter 0.1s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { filter: brightness(1.08); } .ds-btn-primary:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: default; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Low-emphasis action (Cancel, Save in a modal footer).
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { font-family: 'Segoe UI', system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--text); border: 1px solid var(--border); cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background: var(--border); }

components.name: Icon Button
components.description: 26x26px square glyph button for window controls and row actions. Uses a plain Unicode character, never an icon set.
components.css: .ds-icon-btn { width: 26px; height: 26px; border-radius: 6px; display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; background: none; border: none; color: var(--text-dim); font-size: 13px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-icon-btn:hover { background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--text); } .ds-icon-btn.ds-danger:hover { color: var(--danger); }

components.name: Filter Chip
components.description: Multi-select due-date/topic filter pill. The 'on' state borrows its own semantic color on Overdue/Today chips instead of the accent.
components.css: .ds-chip { padding: 3px 9px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--surface-2); border: 1px solid var(--border); font-size: 12px; color: var(--text-dim); cursor: pointer; } .ds-chip:hover { color: var(--text); } .ds-chip-on { background: var(--accent); color: var(--accent-text); border-color: var(--accent); } .ds-chip-on.ds-chip-overdue { background: var(--overdue); border-color: var(--overdue); } .ds-chip-on.ds-chip-today { background: var(--today); border-color: var(--today); }

components.name: Task Card
components.description: The signature component: a 3px left border recolors per due-date bucket, making urgency scannable without reading text.
components.html:
• Finish reportWork
    YesterdayOverdue
components.css: .ds-task { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 10px; background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-left: 3px solid var(--border); border-radius: 8px; list-style: none; } .ds-task:hover { box-shadow: 0 1px 6px var(--shadow); } .ds-task-overdue { border-left-color: var(--overdue); } .ds-task-check { margin-top: 2px; width: 16px; height: 16px; accent-color: var(--accent); cursor: pointer; } .ds-task-body { flex: 1; min-width: 0; } .ds-task-title-row { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 6px; flex-wrap: wrap; } .ds-task-title { font-weight: 600; font-size: 13px; } .ds-task-topic { font-size: 10px; padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--text-dim); border: 1px solid var(--border); } .ds-task-meta { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; margin-top: 3px; font-size: 11px; color: var(--text-dim); } .ds-task-due { color: var(--overdue); font-weight: 600; } .ds-prio-dot { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--prio-high); display: inline-block; } .ds-task-flag { font-size: 10px; font-weight: 700; color: var(--accent-text); background: var(--overdue); padding: 1px 6px; border-radius: 999px; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.04em; }

components.name: Tab
components.description: Top-rounded tab; the active tab fills with the page background so it visually merges into the content below it.
components.css: .ds-tab { padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 8px 8px 0 0; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--text-dim); border: 1px solid transparent; border-bottom: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--text); } .ds-tab-on { color: var(--text); background: var(--bg); border-color: var(--border); }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: Labeled field used throughout the add/edit task form.
components.css: .ds-field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 3px; } .ds-field > span { font-size: 11px; color: var(--text-dim); } .ds-field input { font-family: inherit; font-size: 13px; padding: 6px 8px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid var(--border); background: var(--surface-2); color: var(--text); width: 100%; }

components.name: Modal
components.description: Centered floating dialog for the task form and settings; the only component with real elevation.
components.css: .ds-modal { background: var(--surface); border: 1px solid var(--border); border-radius: 12px; padding: 16px; width: 100%; max-width: 360px; box-shadow: 0 8px 30px var(--shadow); } .ds-modal-title { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; margin: 0 0 2px; }

narrative.overview:
Task Assistant reads like flight-deck instrumentation, not a consumer productivity app: every pixel is informative, color is a signal rather than a decoration, and the whole interface stays small enough to live permanently at the edge of a screen. It is a single-user, local-only tool opened and glanced at dozens of times a day, so the design optimizes aggressively for scan speed and repeat-use efficiency over first-impression polish -- there is no one to onboard and no audience to persuade.

The system is deliberately dense: a 13px base font, a 2-16px spacing rhythm, and a frameless window with custom minimize/maximize/close controls built from plain Unicode glyphs rather than an icon library. Surfaces are flat at rest; the only visual 'weight' in the system is semantic color -- the due-date urgency scale (overdue/today/soon/later) and the priority scale (high/medium/low) do the work that shadows, size, or illustration would do in a more expressive product. This density is the intended standard for future screens, not a placeholder to be loosened.

The visual anti-reference is the mainstream SaaS to-do app: no onboarding carousel, no empty-state illustration, no card-heavy marketing-style spacing, no bespoke icon set, no celebratory animation. Nothing in the system exists to be admired; everything exists to be read in under a second.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, dense, information-first -- color carries meaning, not mood.
One real accent (signal blue) reserved for interactive/selected state; a separate, deliberately distinct color family encodes due-date urgency and task priority.
Plain Unicode glyphs stand in for icons -- no icon font, no SVG set, no image assets.
Flat by default; shadow appears only as a direct response to hover or an overlay (modal).
Frameless window with its own minimal title-bar-equivalent, built from the same component vocabulary as the rest of the app.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue means "interactive or selected," full stop. It never appears as a passive status color, and no other color is used for a clickable/selected state.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: The type scale barely moves (11px-15px); hierarchy is built with weight (400/500/600/700), case, and letter-spacing rather than dramatic size jumps. This keeps the dense layout from feeling chaotic.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Every surface is flat at rest -- no ambient shadows, no resting elevation. Shadow exists only as a direct response to an interaction state.

dos: Do keep Signal Blue exclusively for interactive/selected state -- never repurpose it as a passive status color.
Do keep the due-date urgency scale (overdue/today/soon/later) and the priority scale (high/medium/low) visually distinct, even though both borrow from a red/amber/green vocabulary.
Do keep new surfaces flat at rest; add shadow only as a direct response to hover or an overlay.
Do build hierarchy with weight, case, and letter-spacing before reaching for a larger font size.
Do use plain Unicode glyphs for any new icon need rather than introducing an icon library or SVG set.
donts: Don't add a resting/ambient shadow to any surface -- it breaks the Flat-By-Default Rule.
Don't loosen the spacing scale (2-16px) for a new screen "for breathing room" -- density is the standard, not a gap to fill.
Don't introduce a second brand accent color; there is exactly one (Signal Blue), by design.
Don't add onboarding flows, empty-state illustration, or celebratory motion -- this is a single-user tool with no audience to delight on first use.
